samples.summary: `docs/design/sharing.md` still documents the opposite enforcement default, and builds its whole client-side-gates argument on it
samples.evidence: Lines 208-219: "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode … in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one. That is why the client-side gates are treated as load-bearing throughout this document". Lines 231-235 repeat it ("with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there"). The diff inverts this: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29` returns true unless the value is literally `false`, and `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:158` uses it. This is the design doc a reader consults to decide whether a viewer's write is refused; it is not just prose drift but the stated rationale for treating frontend gates as load-bearing.

samples.summary: Template-gallery design doc still says an unset `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` means the webhook only shadows
samples.evidence: docs/design/template-gallery.md:668 — "with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows* — it logs the decision it would have made and allows the write." After this change, unset enforces (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29`); the reason `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` still demands a literal `true` is now the un-attestable webhook-method registration (as the diff's own `template-review.ts` doc explains), not shadow mode. The doc as written misstates the risk model it exists to justify.

samples.summary: The docs package's read-only store and editor comments still claim the auth webhook ships in shadow mode by default — the notes twin added in this diff was updated, its sibling was not
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42`: "the server-side check behind it — the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one." Same claim at `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4411-4415` ("ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this is the write boundary for a viewer share token"). The new `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` explicitly corrects this reasoning for notes, leaving the two docs-package sites stating the inverse of the new default.

samples.summary: User documentation still says a note opened through a share link has no view menu
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/notes/writing-a-note.md:85-86 — "Like the view mode, the switch is remembered per browser. It isn't available in a note opened through a share link, which has no view menu." `SharedNotesLayout` now mounts `NotesToolbar` on the share route (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:98-115`), which renders the view menu for viewers and, for an editor-role link, the Show-authors switch too (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:549,587`). The published doc now describes behaviour that no longer exists.

samples.summary: Sibling presence write via a raw `doc.update` is not covered by the new `YorkieStore` read-only gate
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:93` sets `activeTabId` presence with a direct `doc.update`, bypassing `YorkieStore`'s new `readOnly` field (which is what suppresses the identical seed at `yorkie-store.ts:111`). I could not find a read-only mount that reaches it — `LakehouseView` is rendered only from the owner route (`document-detail.tsx:720`), and the shared layout mounts `SheetView` alone (`shared-document.tsx:283`) — so this is a latent inconsistency rather than a demonstrated bypass. Confirming would need a share-link/read-only path that can render a lakehouse tab.

finding.summary: Shared slides mount still writes the CRDT root on a viewer mount (`ensureSlidesRoot`), the exact write the diff gates everywhere else — now denied by default
finding.evidence: `slides-view.tsx:282` calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, { initialThemePreference })` unconditionally on every mount, including a viewer-role share link (`shared-document.tsx:502` passes `readOnly` only to `SlidesView`'s editor, not to this call). `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:246` runs a `doc.update()` backfill (`themes`, `masters`, `guides`, `meta.themeId`) on any deck missing those keys, and :229 seeds `meta`/`slides`/`layouts` for an empty one. Per this diff's own reasoning (see `pdf-collab.tsx:200-211`, `yorkie-store.ts:84-96`) a local root change is carried on the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the webhook — now enforcing by DEFAULT (`yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts`) — refuses for a `viewer`, wedging the viewer's whole sync rather than just failing the migration. The pre-existing comment at `slides-view.tsx:276-281` explicitly books this as an accepted "known gap", an acceptance that rested on shadow mode being the default. Second reachable site: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/mobile-slides-view.tsx:147`, mounted for viewers by `SharedMobileSlidesLayout` (`shared-document.tsx:420`, :561) despite that file's comment at :372 asserting it "is never read-only". Fix belongs at these two call sites (gate on the mount's read-only role), not in the new backend code.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass does not exist as described. `slides-view.tsx:285-288` calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, { initialThemePreference: resolvedThemeRef.current, readOnly: readOnlyMount })` — not unconditionally; `readOnlyMount` is defined at `slides-view.tsx:198` from the `readOnly` prop that `shared-document.tsx:502-503` supplies for a viewer share link (`readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, `shared-document.tsx:411`). The second claimed site, `mobile-slides-view.tsx:152-155`, passes `readOnly: mode === "view"`, and `SharedMobileSlidesLayout` mounts it with `mode={readOnly ? "view" : "edit"}` (`shared-document.tsx:626-627`). The helper itself returns immediately for read-only mounts at `yorkie-slides-store.ts:234`, before both the `needsRoot` seed (:241-255) and the themes/masters/guides/`meta.themeId` backfill `doc.update()` (:259-311), so no CRDT root write is issued on a viewer mount. The comment the finding cites as an accepted "known gap" at `slides-view.tsx:276-284` is in fact the new comment describing this very webhook/PushPull hazard and the gate that closes it, and `yorkie-slides-store.ts:218-225` documents the `readOnly` option for the same reason; tests at `packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:79-131` cover the read-only no-op. The finding's quoted evidence (a call with only `initialThemePreference`) is not present at either location.

mergedFrom.summary: Cell comment popover renders on read-only sheet mounts and its handlers write the CRDT root without the new gate

finding.summary: Read-only sheet mounts still write cells: cross-sheet formula recalculation bypasses the new `readOnly` gate in `YorkieStore`
finding.evidence: `sheet-view.tsx:1300` calls `runRemoteSync(true)` unconditionally right after mount (and `:1312` re-runs it on every `remote-change`), which reaches `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` (`packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:963` — no `_readOnly` guard, unlike every other mutator in that file) → `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2964-2980` → `calculate()` → `packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:67/81` `sheet.setCell()/deleteCell()`, which land in `YorkieStore.setCell` (`yorkie-store.ts:~271` `this.doc.update(...)`). The new constructor gate only silences the presence seed, `updateSelection` and `ensureAxisOrder`; the document mutators are untouched, so a share-link viewer opening a sheet that contains any cross-sheet formula issues a root-mutating `doc.update()` — exactly the `rw` PushPull the diff's own comment says the auth webhook refuses, wedging the viewer's sync, and a viewer mutating shared cell data. `recomputeFilterHiddenRows` on the same path (`sheet.ts:1613/1634` `store.setFilterState`) writes too. Fix belongs either on the new gate (guard the write mutators / batch flush when `readOnly`) or at the `runRemoteSync(true)` call sites.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass is not present as described. (1) `sheet-view.tsx:1308` calls `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)`, not `runRemoteSync(true)`; with `needsRecalc === false` the function takes the `sheet.render()` branch (`sheet-view.tsx:1185-1188`) and never invokes `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas`. (2) The `remote-change` handler is likewise gated: `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : needsRecalc(ops))` at `sheet-view.tsx:1322`. (3) The reviewer's central assertion that `packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts` `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` has "no `_readOnly` guard, unlike every other mutator in that file" is false: the guard exists at `spreadsheet.ts:973-976` (`if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }`); line 963 the reviewer cites is doc-comment text, not code. `sheet` in `runRemoteSync` is the `Spreadsheet` view instance (`sheet = s` at `sheet-view.tsx:1027`), so the guarded method is the one called, and the model-level `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (`sheet.ts:2943`) is only reachable through it (`spreadsheet.ts:977`). `_readOnly` is fed from the same prop (`spreadsheet.ts:78`, `sheet-view.tsx:1017`). (4) The secondary `recomputeFilterHiddenRows` claim also fails: it is private (`sheet.ts:1610`) and all callers are mutators; the one on this path is inside `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (`sheet.ts:2976`), short-circuited by the same guard, while the read-only mount path `reloadDimensions()` -> `worksheet.ts:5210-5218` only calls `load*` readers, none of which reach `store.setFilterState`. No `doc.update()` is issued on a read-only mount by this path.
